chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Ethel Waters, Bessie Smith and Ella Fitzgerald
summary: He prefers Ethel Waters, calls Bessie Smith a down-home blues singer and Ella a doll.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Tell me something, I read an article not too long ago that said that Ethel Waters was accepted more by the whites and she was a refined singer and she was a better singer. They were all trying to imply that Ethel Waters was a better singer than Bessie Smith.
Yeah, in my opinion she was.
But did Bessie Smith appeal more to more people?
She was a down home blues singer.
Did she have much more mass appeal than Ethel Waters, I mean as far as black people were concerned?
Yes, but I knew about both, but I was never a jazz buff, (SEVERAL VOICES AT ONCE)
I didn't care about either one of them...
But the thing is, did Bessie Smith have the appeal, the mass appeal of the black people though?
In other words, Bessie Smith was really more representative of the people than Ethel Waters.
During that time I don't know no Negro singer could sing like Ethel Waters and had the personality and still got it, that she's had ever since I've known her.
But would you classify her with Ethel?

Sometimes she gets off. I caught her off twice we just had a little taste in Copenhagen, but nobody was playing then... She slipped just a little bit but she never slipped too much. But Ethel Waters, I just love her.
